technique.how: With the patient sitting, leaning forward, in held end-expiration, listen with the diaphragm at the left sternal border (3rd-4th interspace) and right upper sternal border for a high-pitched, blowing, decrescendo early-diastolic murmur; check for a wide pulse pressure and collapsing pulse. Compare with prior documented examinations to establish that it is new.
technique.prerequisites: Quiet room; prior notes or echo to judge 'new'; note any prosthetic valve.

interpretation.positive_finding: A diastolic murmur is heard in only about 28% of acute aortic dissections and barely changes the odds (LR+ 1.4), but a NEW aortic regurgitation murmur in acute chest/back pain (with pulse deficit or neurological deficit) or in fever/bacteraemia (endocarditis, especially prosthetic valve or IVDU) is a high-consequence finding that demands imaging.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of a diastolic murmur does not lower the probability of dissection or endocarditis meaningfully; most dissections and many endocarditis cases have no regurgitant murmur at presentation.
interpretation.pitfalls: Early diastolic AR murmurs are soft and easily missed in a noisy ED or tachycardic patient; a chronic AR murmur is common in the elderly and is not 'new'. Pulmonary regurgitation and mitral stenosis murmurs can be confused.
interpretation.changes_what: New AR murmur + acute pain: immediate CT angiography/TEE for dissection. New murmur + fever: blood cultures x3 and echocardiography for endocarditis. Absent: no reassurance.

sources.citation: Klompas M. Does this patient have an acute thoracic aortic dissection? JAMA. 2002.
Ohle R, Kareemi HK, Wells G, Perry JJ. Clinical examination for acute aortic dissection: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Acad Emerg Med. 2019.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use the absence of a murmur to exclude dissection or endocarditis; do not attribute a murmur to 'chronic' disease without a prior record.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: New AR murmur with tearing chest/back pain, pulse deficit, hypotension or neurological deficit: activate the dissection pathway (CTA/TEE, cardiothoracic surgery) immediately.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No interobserver data for diastolic murmurs in the dissection or endocarditis literature reviewed.

extraction_notes: Status partially_quantified: Klompas 2002 abstract gives pooled sensitivity (28%) and LR+ (1.4, 95% CI 1.0-2.0) but no specificity or LR-, and the finding was 'diastolic murmur' rather than the id's 'new' murmur. Ohle 2019 (PMID 29265487) abstract reports pooled findings for neurological deficit and hypotension only; the murmur row was not accessible (not in PMC), so no second estimate. No diagnostic-accuracy study of 'new murmur' for infective endocarditis was found ('infective endocarditis new murmur sensitivity diagnosis clinical features prospective' returned 0 hits); the Duke criteria treat new valvular regurgitation as a major criterion (guideline knowledge, unverified recall) and this is reflected in the interpretation text without a number.
